title: [CQ-C03] Optional semantic provider
description:
Objective: Add an isolated Serena read adapter with capability/version discovery and explicit repository-search fallback.

Deliverable: Optional semantic provider. This is task C03 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): C02, R10.

implementationPlan.description:
Implement packages/moe-daemon/src/context/semanticSource.ts, the optional Serena read adapter. It is a library call, invoked OUTSIDE the state mutex like C02's readRepositorySource.

API:
- `export type SemanticQuery = { id: string; purpose: SourcePurpose } & ({ op: 'symbol'; name: string; path?: string } | { op: 'references'; name: string; path: string } | { op: 'overview'; path: string })`.
- `export interface SemanticItem { id; purpose; op; status: SourceItemStatus; reason?: string; tool?: string; content?: string; bytes: number; inconclusive?: true; fallback?: SourceItem }`.
- `export interface SemanticSource { manifest: { commit: string; analyzer: { name: string; version: string; protocolVersion: string } | null }; items: SemanticItem[]; complete: boolean; limitations: string[]; bytes: number }`.
- `export const SEMANTIC_TOOLS = Object.freeze({ symbol: 'find_symbol', references: 'find_referencing_symbols', overview: 'get_symbols_overview' })`. This is the ONLY allowlist passed to openAnalyzerSession: no write, memory or shell tool, ever.
- `export const SEMANTIC_LIMITS`: maxQueries 16, timeBudgetMs 60000 (ceiling 120000), maxResponseBytes 65536, maxTotalBytes 262144. An override outside its range is refused, never clamped.
- `export async function readSemanticSource(projectRoot, commit, queries, options = {})`.
- options holds limits, serenaPath, and test seams: materialize (default C03a materializeCommit), open (default C03b openAnalyzerSession), fallback (default C02 readRepositorySource) and launcher { command, prefixArgs }.

Order of operations:
1. Pure validation BEFORE any IO, throwing invalidInput:
   - commit is a full lowercase id;
   - 1..maxQueries queries with unique ids;
   - op is known and purpose is valid;
   - name is non-empty, at most 200 chars and has no NUL/CR/LF;
   - every path passes C02's normalizedPath rules (exact normalized relative path, no '..');
   - references requires a path.
2. Resolve the analyzer: options.serenaPath, else MOE_SERENA_PATH, else ~/.local/bin/serena ('serena.exe' on win32). It must exist as a file and be executable on POSIX; otherwise the cause is 'analyzer-absent'.
3. materializeCommit(projectRoot, commit). A failure gives cause `materialize-failed:<reason>`.
4. Create a private Serena home with fs.mkdtemp under os.tmpdir(), separate from the materialized dir.
   - Measured 2026-10-29 on Serena 1.6.2.dev0: Serena registers every --project in ~/.serena/serena_config.yml (the 'projects:' list) and keeps memories and logs under its home. SERENA_HOME overrides that home (serena/config/serena_config.py SerenaPaths).
   - When the real <home>/.serena/language_servers exists, link it in as <private>/language_servers (POSIX symlink, Windows junction), so the cached language-server binaries are reused. Nothing else is shared.
5. openAnalyzerSession(launch, Object.values(SEMANTIC_TOOLS)):
   - command: the analyzer or launcher.command; args: [...prefixArgs, 'start-mcp-server', '--context', 'agent', '--project', materialized.dir, '--enable-web-dashboard', 'false', '--enable-gui-log-window', 'false', '--open-web-dashboard', 'false'];
   - cwd = materialized.dir;
   - env = an explicit allowlist copied from process.env when present: PATH, HOME, USERPROFILE, SystemRoot, TEMP, TMP, TMPDIR, LANG, LC_ALL, plus SERENA_HOME = the private home. No MOE_*, GIT_* or credentials;
   - timeoutMs = the remaining budget; maxResponseBytes from limits.
   A failure gives cause `analyzer-failed:<reason>`.
6. Capability check per needed tool, from session.tools:
   - missing gives `capability-missing:<tool>`;
   - the inputSchema.properties must hold the params we send. For symbol, the first of 'name_path_pattern' or 'name_path' (Serena 1.6.2 find_symbol uses name_path_pattern); for references, 'name_path'; and 'relative_path'. Otherwise `capability-mismatch:<tool>`.
7. Per query, call the tool:
   - args: {name_path_pattern|name_path: name, relative_path: path ?? ''}, or {relative_path} for an overview.
   - ok gives 'served' with the text as content and the tool name; truncated gives 'truncated'/'response-byte-cap'.
   - An empty answer is served as returned, never rewritten into a claim of absence.
   - A failure gives cause `tool-failed:<reason>`.
   - Running out of budget gives cause 'time-budget' for that and every later query.
8. Fallback (DoD 1). For every query whose cause is set, the item is 'unavailable' with reason `semantic-unavailable:<cause>`, inconclusive: true, and fallback = the C02 readRepositorySource(projectRoot, commit, ...) item at the SAME commit:
   - symbol and references: a literal search for the name's last '/' segment, scoped to [path] when given;
   - overview: a read of path.
   - Limitations then include 'semantic-unavailable' and 'literal-search-fallback'.
   - A failing fallback is just its own explicit C02 status. Nothing is ever reported as 'helper absent'.
9. Total-byte cap: later items become 'omitted'/'total-byte-cap' with content stripped, using a local loop (do not depend on C02b's capTotal export).
10. complete = every item served. manifest.analyzer = session.server or null.
11. finally, always and once each: session.close(), materialized.dispose(), and rm of the private home (guarded to the created path). A cleanup error is logged, never thrown over the result.

Error handling: hostile analyzer output can only produce statuses. Only caller-shape errors throw.
implementationPlan.note: semanticSource.ts (221 lines) written; tsc --noEmit exit 0 in a Linux HEAD snapshot. API per plan: readSemanticSource, validateSemanticRequest, SEMANTIC_TOOLS, SEMANTIC_LIMITS, SemanticQuery/Item/Source/Options; open/materialize/fallback/launcher stay public options (C04 note), args built in fixed key order. Consumed landed names unchanged: materializeCommit+MATERIALIZE_LIMITS (C03a), openAnalyzerSession (C03b), readRepositorySource+validateSourceRequest (C02). Deviations, each a correctness call: (1) the references fallback searches the whole commit, not just its definition file, which would hide every other caller (the path is still validated through C02). (2) The open handshake and each call race the remaining budget; a session that opens late is still closed. (3) An unexpected seam throw becomes cause 'internal-error' plus fallback, with cleanup intact. (4) The cache link is unlinked before the recursive rm of the private home. (5) item.bytes counts the fallback bytes carried, so the total cap covers both. Validation reuses C02 validateSourceRequest on the derived fallback queries (commit, ids, purposes, paths, literal). The shared tree has 736 dirty paths from other sessions; none touched.

implementationPlan.description:
Write the unit tests in a new packages/moe-daemon/src/context/semanticSource.test.ts, table-driven, using the seams: a fake materialize returning a temp dir, a fake open returning a scripted session, and a call-recording fallback. Run them in a real temp git repo where a fallback needs C02 (repositorySource.test.ts temp-repo pattern, cleaned in afterAll).

Cases. Assert exact status, reason, inconclusive, fallback status and limitations:
- T1: each invalid input throws INVALID_INPUT with ZERO seam calls (bad commit, 0 or 17 queries, a duplicate id, an unknown op, references without a path, a '..' path, a NUL in a name).
- T2: a non-existent serenaPath gives every item 'unavailable'/'semantic-unavailable:analyzer-absent', inconclusive, and a C02 fallback. For a symbol present in the commit, fallback.matches is non-empty. manifest.analyzer is null. Both limitations are present. materialize is never called.
- T3: materialize {ok:false, reason:'boom'} gives 'materialize-failed:boom', and open is never called.
- T4: open {ok:false, reason:'exited:1'} gives 'analyzer-failed:exited:1', and dispose is called exactly once.
- T5: tools lacking find_referencing_symbols send ONLY the references items to fallback ('capability-missing:find_referencing_symbols'); the symbol items are served.
- T6: a find_symbol schema with neither name_path_pattern nor name_path gives 'capability-mismatch:find_symbol'. An old schema that has only name_path is served, and the recorded args use name_path.
- T7: one call {ok:false, reason:'timeout'} gives that item 'semantic-unavailable:tool-failed:timeout'; the others are served.
- T8: a served item carries content, tool and bytes. truncated:true gives 'truncated'/'response-byte-cap'. The allowlist passed to open equals exactly the three SEMANTIC_TOOLS. The recorded args match the mapping.
- T9: an empty answer ('[]') is served unchanged, with no inconclusive flag and no fallback.
- T10: close, dispose and the private-home rm each run exactly once on success, on every failure branch, and when a seam throws unexpectedly. The private home directory no longer exists afterwards.
- T11: the launch env holds only allowlisted keys plus SERENA_HOME. With MOE_WORKER_ID, GIT_DIR and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY stubbed in process.env (vi.stubEnv), none of them reach the env. SERENA_HOME is never the real ~/.serena.
- T12: limits outside their range throw. The budget exhausting mid-run gives 'time-budget' for the remaining items, each with a fallback.

Mutation proof, on a scratch snapshot copy only:
- drop the fallback attach: T2 red;
- invert the capability check: T5/T6 red;
- leak process.env: T11 red;
- skip dispose: T10 red;
- rewrite an empty answer: T9 red.
Record the results.

implementationPlan.description:
Add an integration test (DoD 2 and DoD 3) to semanticSource.test.ts, using the REAL C03a materializeCommit and the REAL C03b openAnalyzerSession against a fake stdio MCP server.

The fake server is a small node script the test writes to a temp file, launched through the launcher seam {command: process.execPath, prefixArgs: [script]}. It:
- answers initialize and tools/list with Serena 1.6.2-shaped inputSchemas;
- implements find_symbol by reading <--project dir>/<relative_path> and returning the lines that contain name_path_pattern;
- ALSO writes <project>/.serena/cache.txt and $SERENA_HOME/serena_config.yml, to mimic Serena's side effects.

Fixture: a temp git repo commits src/util.ts holding `export function helperOld`; the worktree then rewrites the file to `helperNew` (dirty, uncommitted).

Assert:
(a) A symbol query for 'helperOld' is served with the COMMITTED line, and one for 'helperNew' is served empty. The analyzer only ever saw the immutable commit, never the worktree.
(b) After the call, the projectRoot tree, git status --porcelain and .git/index bytes are unchanged, and projectRoot has no .serena directory.
(c) The materialized dir and the private SERENA_HOME no longer exist.
(d) A fake HOME (vi.stubEnv HOME and USERPROFILE to a temp dir) has no .serena written to it. No native knowledge store is recreated anywhere persistent.
(e) The fake server and any grandchild it spawns have exited.
Error handling: any setup failure fails the test with its message; never skip on a failure.
implementationPlan.note:

If ~/.local/bin/serena or MOE_SERENA_PATH exists in the worker environment:

REAL FINDING, FIXED: '.serena' is not in SNAPSHOT_CONTROL_SEGMENTS, so a committed .serena/project.yml was materialized and read by Serena. Its ls_additional_workspace_folders key is not trust-gated (serena_config.py:628) and accepts absolute paths, so a hostile commit could aim the language server at the mutable worktree (breaks DoD 2). activation_command and ls_specific_settings are trust-gated, and the private home's trusted_project_path_patterns is [], so those stay inert. Fix: semanticSource.ts deletes <dir>/.serena (fs.rm, force) before the private home is made and the session opens. An rm failure throws, so it goes down the existing internal-error + fallback path with cleanup.

References served with the src/use.ts callers (tsconfig present). ~/.serena/serena_config.yml sha ac7707af… unchanged; 0 temp leftovers.
- To fit the cap, the analyze loop was collapsed to one line and the test's git/let declarations were merged. Still 203 + 197 = 400 lines.

CHECKLIST:
(1) Absence: every absent, failed, timed-out, capability-missing, mismatched, materialize-failed, home-failed or internal-error path ends as unavailable + inconclusive + a C02 fallback. Empty answers are served as returned, and 'semantic-empty-not-absence' is set whenever a session opened.
(2) Inputs: the analyzer's project and cwd are the private materialized dir only, now with the committed Serena config scrubbed. The allowlist is the three read tools, enforced by C03b. The writer only supplies the commit and query names/paths, which are validated through C02 rules.
(3) Leaks: cleanup runs in reverse on every exit, including throws, and each step's own error is caught. A late session after time-budget is closed asynchronously.
(4) Env: an allowlist plus a private SERENA_HOME (T11).
(5) Fallbacks are labelled 'literal-search-fallback' + 'semantic-unavailable' and carried in item.fallback, never as semantic content.
(6) Forbidden-token grep exits 1 (none).

- The language servers run over committed code with no VM isolation, and none is claimed. tsserver does not load project-local plugins by default.

comments.author: architect-e4b7eee0
comments.content:
Architect note from planning CQ-C03b (task-465fb4b9, now WORKING). These are the client semantics this adapter consumes. All fit inside C03's existing steps.
(1) launch.command MUST be absolute; a relative one throws INVALID_INPUT. The reason: on Windows, libuv runs <cwd>\name.exe before PATH, and cwd is the materialized repository content. In step 2, path.resolve options.serenaPath / MOE_SERENA_PATH, or treat a non-absolute value as 'analyzer-absent' BEFORE the file check, so openAnalyzerSession never throws on it.
(2) maxResponseBytes caps the ANSWER text. Over the cap, the text is cut at a UTF-8 character boundary with truncated:true, which is exactly what your T8 'response-byte-cap' expects. A separate fixed MCP_FRAME_LIMIT_BYTES (4 MiB) caps every JSON line, including tools/list. Only that one fails the session, with 'response-too-large'.
(3) The reason codes you may see, mapped through 'analyzer-failed:<r>' and 'tool-failed:<r>': spawn-failed:<errno>, exited:<code|signal>, protocol-violation, response-too-large, timeout (session-fatal), rpc-error:<code>, tool-error, tool-not-allowed, tool-not-listed, closed.
(4) The client negotiates protocolVersion '2025-06-18', and server.protocolVersion is whatever the server returns. Serena 1.6.2 bundles mcp 1.28.1.

comments.author: architect-e4b7eee0
comments.content:
Architect note, from planning CQ-C04 (task-1b7b6067, plan rev 1). C04 caches semantic answers WITHOUT editing semanticSource.ts. It calls readSemanticSource(projectRoot, commit, queries, { ...options, open: decorated }) and decorates your `open` seam in production code. Please keep:
(1) `open`, `materialize` and `fallback` as public options of readSemanticSource, not test-only internals. open is called as open(launch: AnalyzerLaunch, allowedTools) after materialize, and launch.command and launch.maxResponseBytes are passed through unchanged.
(2) Each query goes through session.call(tool, args) on the session open returned. Build args with a fixed key order; C04 keys answers by them.
(3) ok and !truncated map to 'served'. A failed open or call takes C03's explicit unavailable-plus-fallback path, which C04 never serves from cache.
C04 compares cached and uncached results with JSON.stringify.

Missing prerequisite contract; not REPL silence and not dirty files.

C03 adds an ISOLATED Serena read adapter whose queries consume immutable inputs. The rollout made it depend on CQ-R10 (Isolated agent lifecycle: owned attempt workspaces, scoped credentials, cancellation, fresh-session identity). CQ-R10 is BACKLOG and unplanned, behind CQ-R09, CQ-F10 and CQ-F11. Where the analyzer runs, which immutable workspace it reads and how it is cancelled are CQ-R10 deliverables, so planning now would invent them. This task auto-unblocks when CQ-R10 is DONE.

Then plan against the landed CQ-R10 lifecycle and CQ-C02's landed repositorySource, which supplies the explicit immutable-commit search fallback:
- Capability and version discovery come from MCP initialize plus tools/list, with a read-only tool allowlist.

completionSummary:
CQ-C03 optional semantic provider: new packages/moe-daemon/src/context/semanticSource.ts (203 lines) and semanticSource.test.ts (197 lines, 33 tests), 400 net lines.

API: readSemanticSource(projectRoot, commit, queries, options?) and validateSemanticRequest. Queries are symbol / references / overview, and the three allowlisted Serena read tools (SEMANTIC_TOOLS) answer them. SEMANTIC_LIMITS: 16 queries, 60 s budget (ceiling 120 s), 64 KiB per response, 256 KiB total. Out-of-range limits are refused, never clamped.

How it runs: it materializes the commit privately (C03a), deletes any committed .serena config, makes a private SERENA_HOME that links the shared language_servers cache, and opens the C03b read-only MCP session with an allowlisted env. Every step races the remaining budget. Cleanup runs in reverse on every exit.

Failure handling: any absent analyzer (including a relative command), materialize failure, home failure, open failure, time budget, missing capability, schema mismatch, tool failure or internal error ends as 'unavailable' + inconclusive, carrying a C02 literal fallback at the same commit. A references fallback is unscoped so it finds every caller. Empty answers are served as returned, never rewritten into absence; the 'semantic-empty-not-absence' limitation is set whenever a session opened. Seams (materialize/open/fallback/launcher) stay public for C04, and args are built in a fixed key order.

Self-review fix: '.serena' is not a snapshot control segment, and Serena's ls_additional_workspace_folders is not trust-gated, so a committed project.yml could have pointed the language server at the mutable worktree. Fixed, with a RED mutant test and a real-Serena rerun.
